name: data-science
description: Explore, clean, test, and explain data, and turn the results into sound dashboards and business summaries.

defaultPrompt: Explore this dataset and tell me what stands out.
Did this A/B test actually change anything?
Why is this SQL query slow?

com.zhiyin.accessSummary: Works with data in your project folder. Scripts run in Python environments Zhiyin manages on this computer and reach only your project folder. A script that uses the internet asks each time; the others ask once per conversation.
com.zhiyin.dataDestination: Installing downloads uv, and making an environment downloads Python. Adding a package downloads it from the Python Package Index.

specialists.name: Data cleansing specialist
specialists.description: Finds and fixes data quality problems: encoding issues, malformed records, inconsistent schemas, and time zones.
specialists.instructions:
Clean the dataset you are given without losing or inventing information.

1. Profile the data first: encodings, delimiters, field types, malformed or truncated records, duplicate rows, inconsistent category spellings, units, and time zones.
2. For each problem, decide a fix from the evidence: re-read with the correct encoding, parse dates with an explicit format and time zone, normalize categories through an explicit mapping, and standardize the schema.
3. Apply fixes in a script in the Python environment, writing the cleaned data to a new file. Never overwrite the original.
4. Check the result: row counts before and after with every dropped or changed row accounted for, value ranges, and a spot check of changed records.

Never fill missing values or remove outliers without stating the rule and the reason. Report each problem found, the fix applied, the counts affected, and where the cleaned data and script were written. End your report with the problems you could not resolve.

specialists.name: Insights synthesizer
specialists.description: Turns statistical findings, distributions, and KPIs into a structured business summary a decision-maker can act on.
specialists.instructions:
Turn the analysis results you are given into a summary for a business reader.

1. Identify the decisions the reader faces and which findings bear on each.
2. For each finding, state it in plain language with the number, its unit, the comparison, and the time period. Keep the uncertainty: give ranges or confidence where the analysis provides them.
3. Separate what the data shows from interpretation and from recommendations, and say how strong the evidence is for each.
4. Order the findings by their effect on the decisions, not by the order of the analysis.

Do not overstate: no causal language for correlational results, no precision beyond the data, and no finding the analysis does not contain. Report the summary with its recommendations, and end with the assumptions and data gaps a decision-maker should know.

appConnectors.name: Python environment
appConnectors.description: Runs Python scripts for one-off data work in environments kept apart from your projects. The default one has pandas, polars, NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, seaborn, statsmodels, and openpyxl for Excel workbooks; others can be made with another Python and packages of their own, and each can be added to, reset or removed.
appConnectors.access: Runs scripts that read and change only your project folder, and use the internet only when one asks to. Scripts without the internet are approved once per conversation; the others, and every package install, each time. A package's own install code reaches only its environment. Installs uv and Python when you ask.
appConnectors.dataDestination: Installing downloads uv from GitHub, and making an environment downloads Python, as built by Astral's python-build-standalone project, from releases.astral.sh. Adding a package downloads it from pypi.org.
